disputed: The administration has not itself stated that being transgender, non-Christian, or an LGBTQ+ ally makes someone a 'terrorist' — NSPM-7 and the leaked DOJ implementation memo use broader, vaguer language ('extremism on gender,' 'anti-Christianity,' 'radical gender ideology,' 'hostility towards traditional American views on family, religion, and morality') without explicitly naming these groups. Snopes rated the literal claim 'FBI classified LGBTQ+ people as terrorists' as lacking direct textual support, while noting the vagueness itself is the concern civil liberties groups raise. Whether Antifa functions as a coordinated 'organization' capable of being designated, versus a loose ideological movement, is itself disputed — multiple legal analyses (Brennan Center, Charity & Security Network) say the underlying EO cites no legal basis, since U.S. law does not currently provide a formal domestic terrorist organization designation akin to the foreign terrorist organization list.

items: On September 22, 2025, Trump signed an executive order designating 'Antifa' as a domestic terrorist organization, describing it as a 'militarist, anarchist enterprise' that 'recruits, trains and radicalizes young Americans' and employs 'elaborate means' to conceal funding and operations. The order directs federal agencies to investigate, disrupt, and dismantle Antifa-linked operations and funding sources. (White House Fact Sheet/American Presidency Project; NPR; Ballotpedia)

Legal analysts note the order has no clear legal basis: no U.S. statute currently authorizes designating a domestic 'terrorist organization' the way foreign terrorist organizations can be designated, and Antifa is widely described as a decentralized movement/ideology rather than a formal organization with membership, funding structure, or leadership. (Charity & Security Network; Brennan Center; ICCT)
sections.label: Antifa domestic terrorist designation (Sept. 22, 2025)

items: Three days later, on Sept. 25, 2025, following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, Trump issued National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7), 'Countering Domestic Terrorism and Organized Political Violence.' It lists as 'common threads' or possible indicators of domestic terrorism: 'Anti-Americanism, anti-capitalism, and anti-Christianity'; 'extremism on migration, race, and gender'; and 'hostility towards those who hold traditional American views on family, religion, and morality.' Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller called it the first 'all-of-government effort to dismantle left-wing terrorism.' (ACLU; The Conversation; LGBTQ Nation)

The ACLU and Brennan Center note NSPM-7 does not mention the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack, and argue its broad, vague labels sweep in First Amendment-protected beliefs unconnected to any criminal conduct. A leaked December 4, 2025 DOJ implementation memo (obtained by journalist Ken Klippenstein, reportedly signed by AG Pam Bondi) directs the FBI to compile lists of groups based on views including 'radical gender ideology,' opposition to immigration enforcement, and anti-Christian/anti-American/anti-capitalist sentiment — which Klippenstein characterized as targeting 'anyone who isn't a Trump supporter,' not just the left. (ACLU; Democracy Now; FIRE)

By March 2026, CBS News reported the FBI and IRS had formed a joint initiative ('mission control command center') to investigate nonprofit organizations over suspected domestic-terrorism links, implementing NSPM-7. The FBI's FY2027 budget request separately sought $166 million for a task force explicitly citing 'gender extremism' as a target area, which LGBTQ Nation and Snopes reported was being read by some as classifying transgender people as domestic terrorism threats — a reading neither document states explicitly, per Snopes' review. (Charity & Security Network; LGBTQ Nation; Snopes)
sections.label: NSPM-7 and DOJ implementation (Sept. 2025–Mar. 2026)

summary: Within days of each other in September 2025, Trump designated 'Antifa' a domestic terrorist organization and issued NSPM-7, a memorandum directing federal agencies to treat vaguely-defined views — including 'anti-Christianity,' 'extremism on...gender,' and opposition to 'traditional' family/religion views — as indicators of domestic terrorism, which civil liberties groups warn could be used to target activists, nonprofits, and LGBTQ+ people based on viewpoint rather than conduct.
title: Antifa terrorist designation and NSPM-7 domestic terrorism memo
